title: Self Labs Launches Agent Vault for AI Agent Logins and Payments
summary:
Users can now restrict the financial and access permissions of their AI assistants through a new identity layer from Self Labs. The system, known as Agent Vault, allows AI agents to handle logins and credit card transactions via secure placeholders instead of exposing actual passwords or card numbers. This architecture ensures that sensitive data remains hidden from the AI while the user retains control over spending limits and can require manual approval for specific purchases.

The agentic web identity and privacy stack provided by Self Labs is already utilized by companies such as Google. This new tool is designed for use with agents including Claude Code and Codex, although users must still manually perform bank verification and solve CAPTCHAs to complete transactions. The product is positioned as a critical piece of infrastructure for the expanding AI economy.

selectedTweets.text:
Self is introducing Agent Vault, designed to let AI agents log in and pay for things without being given your actual passwords or card numbers.

Say you’re using Claude Code or Codex. You connect the vault, set a spending limit, block sites you don’t want it using, and decide which purchases need your approval.

The agent uses placeholders instead of your real credentials. The vault handles those details separately when it’s time to log in or pay.

You still have to handle bank verification and CAPTCHAs. https://t.co/wc79wJDxg3
